summary: Provides an XML schema defining the data types used by CLUE, the working group on controlling multiple streams for telepresence. The data model gives a consistent structure for describing the media captures and scenes a telepresence endpoint can offer. It is standards-track.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a form with labeled boxes that a video room fills in to describe its cameras, screens and seating, so another room can read the form and understand it perfectly.

subtitle: The XML schema that lets a telepresence endpoint describe its cameras, microphones, scenes and encodings in a standard way.

tldr.problem: Telepresence endpoints with several cameras, screens and microphones need a precise, shared way to describe what media they can send and what they want to receive.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an XML schema with elements for media captures, capture scenes, scene views, encoding groups, simultaneous sets, global views, people and capture encodings, based on the CLUE framework.
tldr.outcome: CLUE protocol messages use these types so a Media Provider can advertise its offer and a Media Consumer can request streams; extensibility and four IANA registries allow growth.

today: RFC 8846 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2021. It has not been obsoleted or updated, according to the metadata for this entry.

sections.title: Purpose of the CLUE Data Model
sections.content:
CLUE stands for Controlling Multiple Streams for Telepresence, the name of the IETF working group that produced this document and its companions. The schema formally encodes the concepts and constraints of the CLUE framework in RFC 8845.

The data it defines is carried inside CLUE protocol messages (RFC 8847). A Media Provider uses it to advertise its telepresence capabilities as media captures, capture scenes and related features. A Media Consumer uses it to request the options it wants as capture encodings.
sections.plainLanguage: Two video rooms need to describe their equipment in the same language. This document is the dictionary for that language.

sections.title: The Top-Level Structure
sections.content:
The schema's namespace is urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:clue-info. Seven main groups of information sit at the top, each a list of items defined later in the document:

  • <mediaCaptures>: the media captures available.
  • <encodingGroups>: the encoding groups.
  • <captureScenes>: the capture scenes.
  • <simultaneousSets>: sets of captures that can be sent together.
  • <globalViews>: alternative summaries of all scenes offered.
  • <people>: metadata about the participants represented.
  • <captureEncodings>: the instantiated or desired capture encodings.

The <clueInfo> element bundles the first six groups. It exists only for data model testing; it resembles the body of an ADVERTISEMENT message but is not used in the CLUE protocol message definitions. The sample files in the RFC use it.
sections.plainLanguage: The form has a few big sections: what cameras and microphones there are, how they are grouped, which can run together, and who is in the room.

sections.title: Media Captures
sections.content:
A media capture is the fundamental representation of a media flow the provider can offer. The common features live in an abstract mediaCaptureType, and audio, video, text and other captures are specializations of it. Each capture has a mandatory captureID and mediaType (commonly "audio", "video" or "text") and must belong to exactly one capture scene through <captureSceneIDREF>. A capture with no <encGroupIDREF> cannot be instantiated as a stream.

Captures are either spatially definable or not. A spatial capture carries <spatialInformation>: a capture point (with an optional point on the line of capture) and, for video, a <captureArea> of four coplanar points. The point on the line of capture must not equal the capture point. A non-spatial capture, such as a recording or a text capture, is marked <nonSpatiallyDefinable> set to true instead. The two are mutually exclusive.

Optional fields include <description> and <lang>, <priority> (a lower value means more important), <mobility> (static, dynamic or highly-dynamic), <view>, <presentation>, <embeddedText>, <capturedPeople> and <relatedTo>. Audio captures add a <sensitivityPattern> for the microphone.
sections.plainLanguage: Each camera or microphone gets a name tag. The tag says what it records, where it stands in the room and which way it points.

sections.title: Multiple Content Captures
sections.content:
A capture is either individual or a Multiple Content Capture (MCC), which mixes or switches other captures of one media type. An individual capture carries the fixed element <individual> set to true. An MCC can instead carry:

  • <content>: the captures or scene views it is built from.
  • <policy>: a token and index such as SoundLevel:2 or RoundRobin:0. SoundLevel picks the loudest speaker and RoundRobin rotates sources over time.
  • <maxCaptures>: how many captures can appear at once, exact if its exactNumber attribute is true.
  • <allowSubsetChoice>: whether the Consumer may pick a subset; if absent it is false.
  • <synchronizationID>: MCCs with the same value always carry captures from the same sources.

For example, an audio MCC with <maxCaptures> of 4 and exactNumber true always mixes audio from exactly four constituent captures.
sections.plainLanguage: Some captures are a mix, like a TV director who switches between cameras or the loudest speaker. These special captures say how the mix is made.

sections.title: Scenes, Views, Encodings and Sets
sections.content:
A capture scene groups captures that cover a spatial region such as a room. It has a mandatory sceneID and a mandatory scale for its coordinates: mm (millimeters), unknown (same scale, undefined unit) or noscale (no common scale). A scene can list <sceneView> elements, each a set of same-type captures that completely represents the scene.

An encoding group holds a <maxGroupBandwidth> in bits per second and a list of individual encoding IDs that share it. A simultaneous set lists captures of one media type that can be sent at the same time, and may use scene view or scene IDs as shortcuts. A global view summarizes the whole offer using scene view IDs.

The <people> list describes participants with a vCard in <personInfo> and one or more <personType> roles.

On the Consumer side, a <captureEncoding> pairs a <captureID> with an <encodingID>, and for an MCC may add <configuredContent>. It is used in CONFIGURE messages and may not list more captures than the MCC's <maxCaptures>.
sections.plainLanguage: The room is split into scenes, cameras are bundled into views, and a bandwidth budget is shared among them. A request says which camera to send and how to pack it.

sections.title: Extensibility
sections.content:
The model is meant to be extended. Elements or attributes from XML namespaces other than the CLUE and vCard ones may appear wherever the schema allows anyElement or anyAttribute, and elements or attributes from unknown namespaces MUST be ignored. The schema is written to still satisfy the Unique Particle Attribution (UPA) constraint.

The otherCaptureType exists to carry media types defined in extensions. The RFC includes an example extension schema in its own namespace that adds a newAudioFeature to an audio capture and a feature to an otherCaptureType capture.
sections.plainLanguage: The form has blank lines at the bottom. Anyone can add their own questions there, and readers who do not understand them simply skip them.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The security concerns of RFC 8845, Section 15 apply. Data model information carried in CLUE messages SHOULD be accessed only by authenticated endpoints, especially when it carries personal information in <personInfo> vCards or scene information. Authentication is not mandatory, since a session might need no protection at all. Integrity and authentication are left to the transports, namely the CLUE protocol (RFC 8847) and the CLUE data channel (RFC 8850). Parsers must be robust against malformed XML.

IANA registered the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:clue-info, the schema urn:ietf:params:xml:schema:clue-info and the media type application/clue_info+xml. It also created four registries for <view>, <presentation>, <sensitivityPattern> and <personType> values, with new values assigned by Expert Review.
sections.plainLanguage: The form can hold private details about people, so only trusted rooms should read it, and the carrier that delivers it is responsible for locking it.
